status: Independent necessary-condition calculation for strict Euclidean nearest-neighbor realization
source_graph: Same full halfwave Pearson rankings as ANA159; no anatomical graph
assumptions: Distinct map points and strict neighbor boundary; every row selects its closest k eligible points.
One forbidden own-coordinate opponent per row, in addition to self exclusion.
1D Euclidean line or2D Euclidean plane, not a torus, weighted metric, non-Euclidean geometry or variable-k graph.
proof: Partition the line into2rays or plane into6half-open cones of angle60degrees around a candidate target.
If k+2selecting points lie in one cone, choose the farthest. Each of the other k+1points is strictly closer to it than the target is, by the cosine law.
After at most one opponent exclusion, at least k eligible closer points remain. Thus the target cannot be among its k nearest eligible partners, a contradiction.
Hence a target is selected by at most2(k+1)points on a line or6(k+1)in the plane.
If the original count is h_j and the map bound is B, at most min(h_j,B)original edges into j can be preserved. Summing gives the stated recall upper bound.
limits: This necessary condition is loose and does not determine the best achievable map or explain the entire observed loss.
Nearest-neighbor retention is a descriptive diagnostic, not an application requirement.
Variable-degree probabilistic spatial graphs are not subject to this same fixed-k bound; no conflict with the application capacity distribution follows.
This does not prove geometry has no useful computation or select a learning score.
